shop/may

What it is
  What somebody deciding to apply this most needs to know.
  What it is doing is written down as it goes, so that it is taken up where it was after a restart.
  Whoever applies it may tell it 3 things:
    - command: A command of your own. It has to be said.
    - key: The secret the tool is handed. Unless it is said: nothing.
    - spec: Everything the last tool is handed. It has to be said.

What it makes
  A thing called `shelf`. [made]
  Another blueprint, `shop/other`, run under it and waited for. [other]

What it does when it is applied
  1. Run a command and wait for it to finish. [listed]
  2. Run a command and wait for it to finish. [yours]
  3. Run a command and wait for it to finish. [whole]
  4. Make sure a thing is there. [made]
  5. Run `shop/other` and wait for it to finish. [other]
  6. Run a command and wait for it to finish. [script]
  7. Run a command and wait for it to finish. [mixed]

What it may do
  It runs as whoever applies it, and can do no more than they can.
  Of what they can do, it uses only what it lists: `shell`, `things`, `secrets`, `blueprints` and `post`.
  Make and change things. [things:write]
  Start, apply and stop blueprint instances. [blueprints:run]
  Use what the factory keeps secret, without being shown it: hand one to a program. [secrets:use]
  Run commands on a device. [shell]
  Send letters. [post:send]
  ! It runs a command: `git status --short`. [listed]
  ! It runs a command that the param `command` says. [yours]
  ! It runs a command it is handed as it runs, which its text does not write out. [whole]
  ! It runs a command of 2 lines, written out in its text. [script]
  ! It runs a command: `make <the param command> -j<the param key>`. [mixed]
  ! It hands the secret `shop` to what it runs, as the variable `SHOP_TOKEN`.
  ! It hands the secret the param `key` names to what it runs, as the variable `TOOL_KEY`. [yours]
  What the blueprints it starts may do is said of each of them: `shop/other`.
